subject: Mobile Development
title: Smartphones for a Dollar a Day
description: A micro-lesson that makes Smartphones for a Dollar a Day usable.

hook.text: In 2010, the cheapest smartphone cost $200. By 2020, you could buy one for $30.

buildup.text: Chinese manufacturers like Xiaomi sold phones at near cost, making profit on services.

discovery.text: Android One and Android Go optimized the OS to run on phones with just 1GB of RAM.

twist.text: Cheap smartphones brought internet access to billions who had never owned a computer.

climax.text: For most of the world, the first computer they ever used was a $50 smartphone.

punchline.text: A $50 phone is the world's computer.

quiz.question: What did Android Go optimize for?
options: Phones with very low RAM and storage
